display: Accountant at an audit firm in KL, studying part-time for an MBA, and helping my mother's home food business with its books.

signals.text: I'm looking for a wedding reception hall in the KL/Selangor area for about 300 guests, on short notice, and the search is eating my weekdays.
I won't pay a large upfront deposit to a venue again unless I can read their accounts first, so I'm looking for someone who can vet a venue's financial health.
My wedding is about five months away and I still don't have a hall or invitations, so I'm behind on everything that depends on the venue.
A reception venue I booked went into liquidation. I need to file a proof of debt and I'd like to talk to someone who has actually recovered money in a case like this.
My reception budget now has a hard ceiling, so I'm looking for good-value halls or caterers that don't need a big upfront payment.
My mother's kuih business needs proper pricing and receipts, but she's proud and resists advice. I'm looking for ways to get a home-kitchen seller to formalise gently.
I'm worn out in a way coffee doesn't fix. Audit season, an MBA and wedding admin are all piling up, and I'd welcome ideas on how to carry less.
My MBA group assignment in Financial Management is due on 24 October. Two of the five members rarely reply, so I'd like to find reliable people to study with.
I'm trying to get a later start date on a new client engagement at work and to say no more easily. I'd like to learn how others set boundaries with partners and family.
My costing sheets work, but I'd like to hear how other small food sellers handle supplier ledgers, cash payments without receipts, and seasonal pre-orders.
I haven't been eating or sleeping well lately and I'm quietly overloaded. I don't tell many people.

offers.text: I'm an ACCA-qualified accountant with 8 years in SME and manufacturing audit, familiar with Malaysian SST and corporate tax filings.
I can read a small company's financial statements and give a plain-language view of whether it looks stable, which is useful before you hand over a deposit.
I can do per-unit costing and pricing for home-based food businesses, and I've built Excel templates for tray costing, weekly cash-up and supplier ledgers.
I can walk a small business owner through basic bookkeeping set-up: what to record, what to keep receipts for, and how to prepare for an audit or tax filing.
I know how stocktake and inventory-count controls fail at manufacturing sites, and I can explain them in practical terms.
I can help with a valuation or financial-analysis section of an MBA-level case study, especially regional airlines.
I can give weekday-evening favour advice to SME owners through my network of audit colleagues and business owners.
I know how to approach a proof of debt in a company liquidation from the accounting side.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I run a small home bakery and I've never separated my costs from my household money. I don't know whether my cakes are making a profit. Can you help me work out what to charge?
catchers.can: Priya can build a per-unit costing sheet with them, point out where they're underpricing, and share her tray-costing and cash-up templates.
catchers.confirm: Is this a small home-scale food seller who needs help working out costs and pricing, rather than someone who needs a full statutory audit?

catchers.hypo: I'm a small manufacturer in Shah Alam and my stock records never match the physical count. How should I set up a stocktake that an auditor will accept?
catchers.can: Priya can explain practical count controls and what auditors look for, based on her experience at manufacturing clients.
catchers.confirm: Is your issue a mismatch between stock records and physical counts at a Malaysian manufacturing site?

catchers.hypo: I own a function hall in the Klang Valley with a free date in about five months, and I'm happy to show you my accounts and a flexible payment schedule if you're serious.
catchers.can: Priya can view the hall, and she can review the venue's financials herself before committing any deposit.
catchers.confirm: Can the hall hold roughly 300 guests for a morning-to-evening event and accept staged payments rather than a large upfront deposit?

catchers.hypo: My mother does her own accounting in a notebook and pays suppliers in cash with no receipts. She won't listen to me. How do you get a proud parent to formalise?
catchers.can: Priya is dealing with exactly this at home and can share what has and hasn't worked, including starting from the numbers rather than from compliance.
catchers.confirm: Is the person you're trying to help a family member running a small home business who resists changes to how they keep records?

catchers.hypo: Our wedding vendor went bust and we paid a deposit. Has anyone been through the liquidation process, and is it worth filing a claim?
catchers.can: Priya can explain how a proof of debt works and what to expect from an unsecured claim, and her cousin is a lawyer who may be able to give a pointer.
catchers.confirm: Is your vendor in formal liquidation, with a liquidator who has said your deposit is an unsecured claim?

catchers.hypo: I'm a few years out of university and am doing the part-time MBA while working full-time. How do you survive group assignments when half the team goes quiet?
catchers.can: Priya can share how she runs a shared drive and splits sections so that the work gets done, and she may team up with someone reliable.
catchers.confirm: Are you in a part-time, working-professional programme with a group assignment currently in progress?

catchers.hypo: I work in audit and my partner keeps adding files. I can't seem to say no. Do you have any advice?
catchers.can: Priya can talk honestly about negotiating workload and start dates, and about leaning on her fiancé, who is better at saying no.
catchers.confirm: Are you a mid-level professional with a boss who adds work while you're already overloaded, rather than someone facing a formal HR dispute?

catchers.hypo: I'm a caterer and I'd like to bid for a 300-guest Hindu wedding in the Klang Valley this year. Who should I speak to?
catchers.can: Priya can pass the enquiry to herself or to her fiancé to compare quotes, and she'll ask for clear pricing before paying.
catchers.confirm: Do you cater vegetarian-friendly wedding menus for around 300 guests and quote a clear per-head price without a large upfront payment?

forbids.text: I won't lie to clients, bend numbers, or sign off on figures I don't believe, even as a favour to family.
I'm not taking on new weekend work before the wedding.
I'm unavailable on Saturdays until December because of MBA classes.
I won't pay a large upfront deposit to any venue or vendor without seeing their financials.
I can't do audit or tax work for friends' businesses on an unpaid, ongoing basis. My firm's independence rules and my own time don't allow it.

projects.text: I'm finding a reception hall for about 300 guests in KL/Selangor on short notice, with a staged payment schedule. A viewing in Subang is already set for 17 Oct.
roles_needed: someone who can vet a venue's financials

projects.text: I'm helping a home-kitchen kuih business move to proper costing, supplier invoices and pre-order tracking ahead of Deepavali and Hari Raya.
roles_needed: supplier of coconut or gula Melaka that issues receipts

policy.t1: Wedding timeline, the venue search and what I need from a hall, general stress about bookkeeping and workload, and my weekday availability.
policy.t2: That a venue deposit was lost in a liquidation, the budget ceiling for the reception, and the family's cash position.
policy.never: Anyone's health details, my credit card balances, and my emotional breakdowns.
